findings.reason: The approach previously described recursive DFS even though both protected sources advance an iterative list of reachable trie nodes. It now documents the exact literal transition, wildcard expansion, empty-frontier exit, terminal test, and frontier invariant.

The former O(B^L) bound ignored the source constraint of at most two dots and overstated branching at literal positions. Search is now stated as O(L B^d), where d is the dot count, d <= 2, and B <= 26; the iterative frontier uses O(B^d) references within the overall O(T) storage bound.

The former benchmark used digit-containing words outside the lowercase contract, contained no wildcard search despite its claim, and sized by calls rather than characters. Legal five-letter streams now combine one two-dot frontier query with exact queries at 40/320/1,280 processed characters; trie search passes, while a correct stored-word scan passes every output and fails only scaling (+0.61 relative exponent).
